entries.summary: Three items remain uncommenced per the compilation's 'Uncommenced provisions table': (1) Public Health (Consequential Provisions) Act 2016 Pt 5 Div 5; (2) TAB (Disposal) Act 2019 s. 148; (3) Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 ss 7, 8(8), 9(2), 12, 15-19, 20(3), 22-24, 26, 27, 30, 37, 43 and Pt 2 Divs 4-5. entries.summary: State Administrative Tribunal guidance (reported via McLeods Lawyers' commentary, citing Hunter v City of Joondalup [2025] WASAT 36) construes the s. 33H(1)/33I(2)(b) 'satisfied that the dog can be kept without the likelihood of any contravention of this Act' standard as a two-part test: factors going to the dog (breed characteristics, training since the incident, current risk, subsequent incidents) AND factors going to the person liable for its control (insight into the causes of the earlier behaviour, compliance history, cooperation with authorities). Onus rests on the applicant seeking revocation, and the Supreme Court is reported as directing that local governments reassess declarations against the most up-to-date material rather than resting solely on the original incident.

provenance.source: McLeods Lawyers, 'Review of dangerous dog declarations made under the Dog Act 1976'
provenance.citation: Hunter v City of Joondalup [2025] WASAT 36, as summarised by McLeods Lawyers
provenance.quote: a dog's behaviour is generally reflective of the ability of the person liable for the control of the dog to exercise effective control over and manage the dog

entries.disposition_note: The s. 33H/33I 'satisfaction' standard is encoded as a fact-supplied input (the decision-maker's own evaluative determination — see fork F-33H-SATISFACTION-STANDARD) rather than computed, and the input field's @desc and an inline @ref cite this guidance so a reader sees what the evaluative standard is meant to weigh, without the encoding purporting to compute an outcome no algorithm should.
